svg.text: The two-stage AI security response: cheap detection, expensive thinking — only when it matters
Stage 1 = the always-on sorter · Stage 2 = the reasoning agent, fired only when Stage 1 flags · edge-to-core triage
AWS: GuardDuty ML · OSS: ML Commons
the 99.9% of events that are business
its keep here — nothing is dropped.
STAGE 2 · THINK + ACT — only on anomaly (LLM tokens spent here, nowhere else)
LLM triage: cents per call — spent only on
the ~0.1% of events the sorter flags.
An LLM on raw streams: too slow, too
# process dies, container survives for forensics — no app downtime
the sensor side of the loop:
feed Stage 1 make the kill precise.
The guardrail that makes the automation safe
the agent gets a read-mostly tool catalog (query findings, read policies) — irreversible actions (kill a container, blackhole egress) stay policy-gated or two-step.
every automated action writes an audit event. An ML finding always carries confidence + model_version and ADDS to the rule layer — it never replaces it.
The LLM is the orchestrator, never the sensor.

AWS chain: GuardDuty (incl. AI Protection) → EventBridge → Step Functions → Bedrock Agent → Lambda → eBPF | OSS chain: ML Commons detector → results index → alerting → agents (plan-execute-reflect) → tool
